mode: Read-only source correctness review; no builds, tests, Docker actions or source edits during review
scope: Optimized asynchronous relay, bounded immutable batch state, fenced atomic result persistence and sampled admission protocol
checks: One relay coordinator per instance; claim size is capped by currently available actual-send permits.
Permit acquisition precedes send; callback or synchronous throw releases once. Timeout/freeze does not release actual-send permits, so later batches retain the shared outstanding bound.
Callback state is synchronized and keyed by logical event plus claim generation. First terminal outcome wins, invalid ACK cannot publish, and frozen or cancelled snapshots reject later callbacks.
Unknown submitted outcomes become AMBIGUOUS; never-started records become TRANSIENT BATCH_NOT_SENT. Neither classification discards durable eligibility.
Callbacks perform no SQL or fault hooks. ACK hooks and status persistence run on the coordinator after immutable result capture.

Claim renewal and settlement use event identity, claim token, CLAIMED status and live database lease predicates. Database guards independently prevent expired ownership overwrite and immutable delivery-history changes.

One bounded status UPDATE executes inside TransactionTemplate. Applied IDs and publication success counts are used only after transaction completion; statement and COMMIT failures preserve retry safety.

Shutdown fences further coordinator work, interrupts the active coordinator, closes producer work and leaves unresolved claims recoverable. A commit already in progress may safely finish for its acknowledged results.

Admission is checked after existing-key replay/conflict arbitration and before financial mutation. Denial rolls back a new reservation; overload and unavailable/stale status responses retain 503 plus Retry-After and same-key retry semantics.

Disabled admission performs no sample query. Enabled admission keeps previous evidence on query failure, uses monotonic freshness, rejects unknown/stale evidence and applies hysteresis to both publication and consumption backlog.

Consumer auto-commit remains disabled; only the individual delivery offset+1 follows durable DB outcome. Revocation commits nothing, paused heartbeat records are sought back, and redelivery remains protected by the durable inbox.
confidenceLimits: Source review and finite executed schedules do not prove every JVM/OS/network interleaving. Existing full92 test-phase pass and focused10 pass are separate evidence; no new tests were executed by this review.
Producer construction holds a lifecycle monitor and can wait on OS/JVM bootstrap DNS. The tested shutdown bound does not establish a universal bound for arbitrary resolver stalls.

Expired owners may still send to Kafka; generation fencing protects PostgreSQL publication evidence, while durable inbox uniqueness protects the defined projection effect. Transport duplicates remain intentional.

Admission is local and sampled best effort. Concurrent requests may overshoot thresholds; it is not a hard global queue cap. Query cost includes historical outbox/inbox rows and larger-history scalability is not established by this review.

A network error during COMMIT can leave an unknown server outcome; no optimistic metric or result is assumed. A committed status is immutable, while a noncommitted claim remains eligible after lease expiry.
existingEvidence: /private/tmp/tpp-phase3-full-verify.log (92-test phase pass; first static phase failed before separate fixes)

postReviewCorrection.status: Applied in1737a27 after all timed benchmarks. Deterministic regression failed against measured production and passed after correction; final clean suite gate and final runtime acceptance remain separate.
postReviewCorrection.defect: An admitted start may read stopInProgress=false before stop CAS, then overwrite eager stop flags/install a worker while stop waits for this monitor. Stop originally captured only the old worker outside the monitor and could return with the new worker alive.
postReviewCorrection.correction: Retain eager stop flags and initial interrupts. Inside synchronized(this), reassert stopped flags, recapture current coordinator/worker and detach producer; interrupt current captures and close/join outside the monitor using the existing combined deadline.
postReviewCorrection.regression: Test-only reflective writes under the lifecycle monitor explicitly model the admitted-start scheduling window; verify current worker interrupted/terminated and stopped state. Subsequent same-instance restart must publish a real new HTTP completion to Kafka with one final DB projection and reconciled ledger.
postReviewCorrection.provenanceLimit: Active benchmark image/source remains unchanged. This lifecycle-only correction and final correctness gate must be identified separately in final provenance.
